_readme: Derived bulleted summaries of each row's human-reviewed rationale. Presentation layer only — institutions.json is never modified. Each bullet is compressed from that row's rationale text and introduces no new facts. The full reviewed rationale remains available in the drill-down.

CalSTRS: Most governance-advanced public pension per its own peer research
GenAI policy, cost-benefit analysis and a prioritized pipeline of 25 scoped scalable use cases in place
Explicitly following a governance-first, deploy-later approach
Stops short of scaling: preconditions for scaling met, but no firm-wide production yet
CalPERS: January 2026 board education day featured a Jefferies macro briefing, 'AI: What We Need to Know', covering AI fundamentals, economics and geopolitics
AI treated as an investment and market topic, not internal use
Stops short of piloting: no public GenAI policy, use-case pipeline, pilot or deployment as of early 2026, roughly a stage behind CalSTRS
NBIM (Norges Bank Investment Management): About 50% of 700 staff build their own Claude-based tools in production for screening, ESG and risk monitoring across 7,000 holdings, and meeting prep
Three-year firm-wide push with AI teams, ambassadors and mandatory training
Stops short of embedded: AI cannot make autonomous investment decisions, and human oversight is non-negotiable
CPP Investments: ChatGPT Enterprise deployed to about 1,800 of 2,000 eligible staff: 83% activation, 84% sustained weekly use in 90 days
528 custom GPTs built, 99th percentile against an industry median of 18
Agent-versus-human experiments on real tasks including portfolio reconciliation, attribution and tariff scenarios, under a five-gate governance framework
Stops short of embedded: humans still frame and verify every output, and org structure is not yet redesigned
GIC: Enterprise-wide ChatGIC, a secure ChatGPT, since 2023

Production AI in trading: LLMs processing Bloomberg broker-commentary streams cross-referenced with PM positions, AI-processed broker quotes and ECM deal emails, semi-automated OTC RFQs, global algo wheels, and trader 'vibe coding' in a secure environment
Self-describes as an 'early adopter' embedding AI 'across operations'

Strongest evidence is trading-desk-specific and firm-wide penetration metrics are absent, so the scaling call rests on depth in the core investment function rather than disclosed org-wide adoption rates
BlackRock: Asimov (2024), an agentic investment-research platform autonomously monitoring theses from filings, earnings and research, used by about 150 fundamental-equity staff and scaling to other divisions
RockAI no-code agent platform rolled out to 5,000 in-house developers with firm-wide 'citizen developer' intent, and 50-plus internal teams contributing agents
Production AI in client intelligence, legal and HR; AI Labs unit since 2018 and a named executive AI sponsor
Stops short of embedded: an executive says the reimagined-workflow future 'isn't quite here yet' and 'no one has cracked the nut'
Temasek: 'Winnow' investment super-app built ground-up with investment teams, aggregating internal and external data and ESG intelligence on prospective investments
Knowledge Graph mapping portfolio relationships, and a firm-wide 'AI and digital fluency' program spanning investment, O&P, risk, audit, legal and cyber
Governed via a 'thin layer' over OpenAI and Google models; the CDO frames AI as augmentation, spotting pitfalls and reducing human bias, not automating decisions
Stops short of scaling: no public penetration metrics, and more augmentation-framed and less quantified than NBIM, CPP and GIC
Vanguard: Decade-plus of AI use, deliberately shifted from 'experimentation to impact' after GenAI
Production tools across functions: Crew Assist for contact centers on Azure OpenAI, Client-Ready Article Summaries, and Stress Testing
Documented return of about $500M, per MIT SMR
Firm-wide structure of top-down 'AI champions' across client-facing, HR, legal and compliance, plus bottom-up 'digital ambassadors'
Stops short of embedded: the CIO's own assist-augment-action framework places Vanguard at 'augment', with autonomous 'action' explicitly still ahead
Bridgewater Associates: AIA Labs, formed early 2023 and led by Co-CIO Greg Jensen, runs AI as production infrastructure inside the investment process

AIA macro strategy went live late 2023 on a roughly $100M Pure Alpha sleeve, launched as a standalone roughly $2B fund in July 2024 using OpenAI, Anthropic and Perplexity models alongside proprietary systems, and managed about $4.5B at 11.3% annualized since inception as of July 2026
Own site adds an AIA Forecaster and Pocket Analyst Tool (undated company claim); a fine-tuned Qwen3-235B document-triage model is published but its production deployment is not publicly confirmed
Stops short of embedded: humans retain risk management, data acquisition and trade execution, so AI decides inside human guardrails, and no public evidence shows the org redesigned around AI
Man Group: AlphaGPT, Man Numeric's agentic system for generating, coding and backtesting quant signals, had produced several dozen signals approved for live trading by July 2025, running inside the same Investment Committee validation as human-generated strategies

CIO put generative-AI adoption above 70% of employees in July 2024 (company claim), with GitHub Copilot for prototyping, ChatGPT being tested for document data extraction and hypothesis generation, and internal chatbots over Man's own codebase
February 2026 Anthropic partnership named AI a firm-wide priority, putting Claude and Claude Code in front of portfolio-management teams globally

Stops short of embedded: Man states the system operates with substantial human oversight and 'we can't leave it unsupervised just yet', humans keep strategic direction and final decision-making, and no public evidence shows an org redesign
AQR Capital Management: Two dedicated ML strategies, Turing Equities and Turing Macro, launched 2023 and opened to outside capital in 2025

Bloomberg reported April 2025 that machine learning powers about a fifth of trading signals in the flagship multi-strategy fund (company claim, not independently audited), alongside ML parsing of earnings-call transcripts and AI-assisted internal coding
Co-founder Cliff Asness says on the record that AQR lets the machine decide more and that AI took over combining and weighting factors, 'annoyingly better than me'
Form ADV brochure filed 2026-03-31 states the firm uses machine learning, NLP and other AI tools in support of investment management, giving T1 regulatory corroboration

Stops short of embedded: no public source shows the org redesigned around AI or decisions with no human in the loop, and a March 2026 Forbes profile has insiders calling AI 'evolutionary, not revolutionary'
Schroders: Genie, its first proprietary GenAI assistant, rolled out April 2023 and used daily by over 1,000 colleagues (company claim)
First Cut, a custom GPT producing first-pass company analysis, above 80% adoption across investment desks and saving an average 50 minutes per investor per day as of June 2025 (company claim)

ContextAI screens company reports against roughly 200 sustainability questions; GAiiA, an internal-only GenAI investment analyst, in production since June 2024 for Schroders Capital private-equity due diligence and draft memos

Stops short of embedded: GAiiA runs under 'continual and extensive human oversight', investors must check First Cut and ContextAI results, the one agentic system disclosed was a labelled prototype in June 2025, and no source shows an org redesign
T. Rowe Price: Investment professionals use Chat TRP, rolled out as 'Investor Copilot' within months of late-2022 LLMs, plus predictive analytics and NLP on tasks such as analyzing earnings calls
Chief data office has an LLM in live use structuring metadata to about 80% before a human finishes, atop 1,000-plus net-new data quality rules and board-approved data quality scorecards (2024)
August 2026 announcement created an Investment AI Solutions organization, T. Rowe Price Labs, and an enterprise AI and model risk governance function reporting to the chief risk officer

Stops short of embedded: the firm's published position requires 'clear boundaries between full automation and human sign-off', and agentic work is described as experimentation and as something that 'should occur this year'
Confidence held at med: the only penetration figures, 130-plus AI solutions and associate adoption above 70%, came from the Q2 2026 earnings call, with no retrievable transcript
Balyasny Asset Management: Dedicated Applied AI team under Chief AI Officer Charlie Flanagan, staffed with researchers hired out of Google

BAM ChatGPT, a proprietary assistant that proactively pushes information to portfolio managers, available to employees June 2023; BAM Embeddings, published November 2024, reported beating OpenAI on FinanceBench, 55% versus 47% (company claim)

Firm names 'firm-wide deployment' among four AI principles, with tools embedded in team-level workflows; OpenAI's March 2026 customer story reports roughly 95% of about 180 investment teams actively using the platform, with a Central Bank Speech Analyst cutting scenario analysis from about two days to roughly 30 minutes

Stops short of embedded: every public description is augmentation, with no source showing AI making investment decisions without a human in the loop, or the organisation rebuilt around AI rather than an Applied AI team bolted on
MacArthur Foundation: First internal policy for the Use of Artificial Intelligence established 2023 and published, standing up a presidentially appointed AI Tool Recommendation and Use Committee (AIRUC) that approves proposed AI uses and maintains a use library

Staff usage stays pocketed: analysing standard operating procedures for bottlenecks, reformatting data, identifying patterns, reviewing archives, chatbots to pressure-test strategy, and scenario planning
Reports 'most respondents have saved time using AI tools' in a staff survey (company claim, with no penetration figure, no daily-use claim and no named tool)

Stops short of piloting: its February 2026 account frames the past two years as 'guardrails, pilots, and exploration' and puts 'connecting governance and operations' in the next two, and the policy prohibits AI for grantmaking and hiring decisions
PGGM: Customer-contact operation runs a live pipeline converting calls to text with one AI model, summarising with a second and quality-checking with an automated 'LLM judge'

Firm-wide tooling under a named 'AI Accelerator' programme: over 70% of colleagues have worked with Microsoft Copilot, 20% use one or more of 90-plus internal AI assistants, and around 700 colleagues use the PGGM Intelligent Agent monthly (company claim)

IPE reported October 2024 that PGGM uses LLMs in ESG, generative AI in forecasting and ChatGPT for coding, without deployment detail; governance is still being built, with EU AI Act integration a future objective

Stops short of scaling: customer service is the only department publicly named in production, penetration figures are cumulative or monthly rather than daily, and PGGM places itself in a first phase where AI is a smart assistant
OMERS: Own board and committee summaries record a Trusted AI Policy approved by the Member Services Committee in Q4 2024 and revised twice through May 2025, establishing the AI Governance Program

At the Canadian Investment Review's 2026 Global Investment Conference, Mo Mirza disclosed an internally built AI platform, launched 'last May', now running up to 39 applications in production with more than 1,300 users and developers (company claim)
Adoption managed through stakeholder feedback loops and technical controls

Stops short of scaling: the figures rest on a single conference account characterizing the platform as seeing 'early adoption', no source discloses investment-team penetration, a named investment use case or firm-wide rollout, and the most recent automation case study still described embedding AI as exploratory
BCI (British Columbia Investment Managem: Multiple AI use cases in daily production across investment and operations, named a strategic priority by its own executives

Microsoft customer story records Copilot licences rotated from 300 to more than 570 users including the C-suite, with CTO Tony Payne citing over 22 solutions, over 2,300 person-hours saved, a 30% cut in audit-report writing effort, and an internal survey where 84% of respondents reported a 10-20% productivity increase (BCI's own survey in a vendor story)

Own site describes AI agents in portfolio data software, a natural language interface over an infrastructure and renewable-resources dataset, forecasting models, bottom-up valuation and drafting deal alerts and memos, GenAI accessible to all global employees, and an in-house platform automating the full invoice lifecycle
Stops short of embedded: every source frames the tools as augmenting named human professionals, with no autonomous investment decision or org redesign described
HOOPP (Healthcare of Ontario Pension Pla: Own CTO Q&A (2024) states AI is 'infused in some of our systems and processes', such as robotic process automation and information security tools, with Microsoft Copilot 'recently launched' and a HOOPP AI Lab also confirmed by the 2024 annual-results release
Appointed Damien Steel Chief Technology, Data and AI Officer in mid-2026, the only Maple 8 institution with AI in a top-level title

The Logic reports roughly 1,100 staff can choose ChatGPT, Claude or Microsoft Copilot, a live AI sandbox, and deal teams tracing downstream effects of major events, including a tool built with AI code generation used to monitor the Iran war's market impacts (company claims; Steel states humans make all capital-allocation decisions)
Stops short of scaling: the same profile makes adoption the current project rather than the accomplished state, with soft adoption metrics and forward-looking flagship initiatives
National Pension Service (NPS): Own September 2025 release announces an AI and Innovation Task Force led by its planning director, organized into four divisions: pension and welfare, fund management, institutional operations, and systems
The task force is to establish a top decision-making body and designate a Chief AI Officer, building the framework for an AI transformation

A June 2026 release reports NPS was the first public institution to establish an AI technology cooperation framework with Kakao and secure high-performance GPUs, which is compute and partnership build-out rather than a deployed use case

Stops short of piloting: no public source names a single pilot or limited deployment running inside the investment process, fund management appears only as one task-force workstream, and both releases' forward-looking framing counts as intent
Confidence held at med: both supporting sources are NPS's own releases, with no independent corroboration obtainable
ATP (Arbejdsmarkedets Tillægspension): Only confirmed operational deployment is a generative-AI assistant that drafts call-summary notes for customer advisors

Own 2025-11-25 release reports it live about six months across roughly 300 advisors in the Pensions and Family Benefits divisions, expanding to about 600, with every note reviewed and corrected by a human
Projects savings of more than 16,000 staff hours a year (ATP's own projection, no independent corroboration found)

In June 2025, on becoming a founding partner of Denmark's AI Competence Pact, ATP stated AI already plays a significant role across all customer service and case processing, and committed to upskill employees

Stops short of scaling: one production use case confirmed, confined to two administrative divisions rather than the firm as a whole, and no public source shows AI in daily production inside the investment process at all
MassPRIM (Massachusetts Pension Reserves: Public AI record is intent, not deployment

2024 objectives were to explore 'incorporating AI into PRIM's business processes and evaluate potential solutions' and to examine applications of large language models in investment analysis and monitoring, with staffers calling the work 'baby steps'

Coverage of the February 2025 annual board meeting states only that PRIM began exploring uses for AI and wants to continue exploring applications in 2025; fiscal-2026 results coverage from 4 August 2026 carries no operational AI update
Stops short of piloting: no source names a shipped pilot, a limited deployment in any team, an AI use policy or a governance committee, so neither half of the piloting bar is met
Confidence held at med: both supporting articles come from the same outlet and author, and PRIM's own board materials could not be read
Franklin Templeton: November 2025 Wand AI partnership release states the firm spent the past year 'evolving from pilot programs to production deployments of intelligent agents across multiple departments', with initial implementation focused on priority use cases within investment teams (first-party, uncorroborated)
Head of AI Platform Vasundhara Chetluru says the partnership 'brings agentic AI out of the lab and into live production'

January 2026 launch of Intelligence Hub, an AI-driven distribution platform on Microsoft Azure, to U.S. Distribution teams, described as production-ready after a multi-month pilot with reduced daily preparation time

Stops short of embedded: no source shows AI making investment decisions without a human in the loop or the organisation redesigned around AI, agents are framed as supporting research and efficiency, and the firm-wide ambition is future tense, with agents 'expected to be used' in key enterprise workflows by 2026
EQT: Own domain documents Motherbrain as firm-wide production tooling: a May 2024 post names deal management workflow, market analysis and monitoring, and talent sourcing, and says it lets anyone manage pipelines, add assessments and track advisors

A July 2025 post says 'AI is already embedded in much of our infrastructure', naming automated due diligence and modeling, and describes a roadmap requiring AI literacy across investment professionals (first-party, uncorroborated)

The same post caps the call: 20% of investment-professional users represent the lion's share of AI-connected prompts in Q1 2025, so daily generative-AI use is concentrated and the row rests on Motherbrain's deployment

Stops short of embedded: EQT states it is 'still unlikely that machines will fully automate investment decisions', Motherbrain ranks opportunities for a human to decide on, and the roughly 35-person AI transformation team Reuters reported in May 2026 is additive headcount, not structural redesign
Amundi: COO Guillaume Lesage states all employees have access to the ALTO Studio platform, half use it weekly, and the firm has 20 real applications to asset management (first-party, uncorroborated)
The single named example is compliance software letting a marketer check that a proposal is compliant

Amundi's Compliance Assistance tool, built on ALTO Studio, won 'The Most Promising Project Using Gen AI' at the AM Tech Day Awards on 8 October 2024, and WatersTechnology reported in March 2025 that ALTO Studio has 500 users among researchers, quants and financial analysts

Stops short of scaling: the only penetration figure is weekly rather than daily use by about half of staff, exactly one of the claimed 20 applications is named, the agentic layer is 'the latest development to come', and no source names AI a formal strategic priority
Citadel: Citadel LLC, the multi-strategy hedge fund, distinct from the separately run market maker Citadel Securities, has at least two named AI systems in production for investment staff

The internally built Citadel AI Assistant, trained on licensed transcripts, regulatory filings, brokerage research and the firm's own strategies, was reported in December 2025 to surface risks and generate tailored research, with regular use across almost all equities investors (company claim via CTO Umesh Subramanian)
By May 2026 Head of Core Engineering Atte Lahtiranta described analysts using Claude for Excel to build and update coverage models and pressure-test their work (company claim)

Stops short of embedded: Subramanian cautioned that investment decisions remain for humans, no public evidence shows decisions taken without a human or the organisation redesigned; confidence held at med as the penetration figure is scoped to equities investors and citadel.com returned 403
Two Sigma: February 2025 Q&A has AI Core Team head Mike Schuster describing scientists prompting LLMs to pull twenty years of Fed speeches and earnings-call transcripts and map them onto subsequent interest-rate moves; generative AI used for well over five years, NLP over a decade (company claim)
By January 2026 CTO Jeff Wecker wrote that 'everyone at Two Sigma is expected to use LLMs to accelerate their work'

A dedicated AI and machine learning team was created in May 2024 to define and implement firm-wide AI/ML strategy, and its leader was promoted that August to Chief Investment Officer of Two Sigma Investments

Stops short of embedded: human scientists still frame the question and verify the output, with no evidence of decisions without a human or of restructuring; confidence held at med as claims are self-published with no penetration metric
CSOP Asset Management: Two Microsoft releases sixteen months apart document daily production across functions: by May 2024 a bespoke Azure OpenAI chatbot and email pre-classification were live for sales, senior management, HR and the operations middle office, credited with 20% better information retrieval and filtering out 80% of non-essential correspondence (company claims)

By September 2025 an 'Intelligence Hub' on Azure AI Foundry and GitHub Copilot carried three named production tools: an ETF reporting portal (10 minutes to 30 seconds), trade-data extraction, and an analytics tool built by Deputy CEO and CIO Yi Wang generating trading ideas for internal reference
Governance is a deployment gate rather than a published policy: IT review for security, compliance and core AI principles

Stops short of embedded: humans make the call on the investment tool's ideas, with no autonomous decisions or org redesign shown; confidence held at med as every fact rests on Microsoft-authored vendor pages
State Street Investment Management (SSGA: Own January 2026 article by the Global Head of Research and Head of Data and Analytics states ML and AI are integral to the investment process, from trading to forecasting
AI-powered chatbot available to investment teams as a research assistant; Systematic Equity runs NLP factors, including neural-network embeddings, over earnings-call transcripts and filings

Corporation-level earnings calls report a centralized AI hub with over 200 use cases and 70 live, near-universal employee access, and agentic copilot delivered to all eligible employees, never broken out by division
Confidence med: the investment-process evidence rests on one first-party article with no corroboration and no disclosed adoption metric

Stops short of embedded: firm says AI amplifies rather than replaces human judgement, is not yet comfortable using generative AI for direct investment modeling, and its XGBoost fundamentals forecaster is not implemented in live portfolios
Millennium Management: Anthropic's August 2026 announcement says Claude and Claude Code are used broadly across Millennium today, spanning trading desks, engineering and core functions across the firm's 340+ investment teams
Millennium's own February 2026 interview names a second system in service: an internally built search platform for proprietary content that developers can integrate into their applications
Structure behind the priority: a Global Head of AI, Technology since October 2023, centralized and federated AI teams, and a global AI lab announced June 2026
Confidence med: every adoption claim is first-party, with no independent reporting of penetration, daily use or a named investment-process use case

Stops short of embedded: the digital risk analyst co-developed with Anthropic is still being built and piloted, logs its reasoning, tests actions in sandboxes, and requires human experts to approve decisions
Fidelity Investments: Chief Investment Officer reported October 2023 that Saifr, introduced by Fidelity Labs, is used by portfolio managers, sales and other staff to flag brand, reputational and regulatory risk in communications as they are drafted
Fidelity also runs materials for funds it is launching through the same tool

AWS's re:Invent 2025 write-up records an enterprise-scale text-to-SQL system, 93-95% execution accuracy and about 28-second responses, letting non-technical staff query internal databases in natural language

Stops short of scaling: AWS describes a capability showcased at a conference rather than stated in production, the trade piece is framed around what staff can do with no user count or deployment date, no source puts AI inside the investment process, and the governance leg is unevidenced
PGIM: Prudential's newsroom reports a shipped sales chatbot for PGIM Global Wealth wholesalers that had handled nearly 5,000 queries as of May 2026, returning fund placement, performance, fee and commission data in seconds
Same first-party page states a Responsible AI framework governing deployment across Prudential, per-use-case regulatory evaluation, and humans at the helm for consequential decisions
WatersTechnology reported December 2023 that PGIM Quantitative Solutions was building an NLP-based physical climate risk index; described as being built and never confirmed shipped, so read as intent

Stops short of scaling: the only production-confirmed tool is sales support contained to one team, no source shows multiple use cases in daily firm-wide production across research, portfolio construction, risk or trading, and none names AI a firm-wide priority with deployment evidence
Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB): Microsoft's customer story documents two shipped systems: Microsoft 365 Copilot deployed to staff with prompt-engineering training workshops, PNB among the first Copilot deployments in Malaysia
SuperApp, an Azure OpenAI knowledge advisor integrated with Teams, answers employees' HR-policy questions across departments, replacing lookups of 15 to 30 minutes; vendor-carried company claim
Microsoft Asia's July 2025 feature shows the rollout still live roughly eight months on, profiling a Technology Department employee drafting documents, building slides and summarising meetings
Governance thin: the Group CFO describes permissioned access only, with no AI use policy or governance committee publicly disclosed

Stops short of scaling: no headcount, adoption percentage or firm-wide scope disclosed, both use cases sit in enterprise productivity and HR rather than the investment process, and the CTO and CFO investment-side language is conditional, read as intent
M&G: Microsoft customer story dated June 2025 records Microsoft 365 Copilot going from 300 licensed pilot users to 600 staff, and GitHub Copilot credited with 11% of a 22% development-time reduction
PRAI, an AI code-review tool, scanned over 2 million lines of code and flagged 3,500 issues in five months; Head of Performance Oversight reports 25% less touch time on customer inquiries

WatersTechnology reports M&G Investments moving equity research to Bloomberg Research Management Solutions, an AI research engine over more than 400 million company documents, after building a data lake
M&G's own site describes a standing cross-functional AI Governance Forum that reviews and evaluates AI use cases

Stops short of scaling: 600 Copilot users is a pocket, the vendor page frames the rollout as still expanding, Bloomberg RMS augments research rather than making live decisions, and three fetched results announcements mention no AI at all
AllianceBernstein: WatersTechnology reported December 2023 that AB had boosted the accuracy of its generative AI models to 95%, fine-tuning that implies deployed models being measured
July 2024 firm-wide Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer role for Andrew Chin, an operating-committee member placed under the COO rather than a technology executive
COO Karl Sprules framed the appointment around AI enhancing investment-research, operational and business procedures; a company claim naming no underlying use cases or their reach
Fortune's September 2025 profile corroborates the reporting line and deliberate placement, but its most concrete statement is forward-looking about reimagining workflows
Stops short of scaling: no source names multiple production use cases, gives a user or penetration figure, or shows daily firm-wide use
Ares Management: February 2026 conference transcript: CEO Michael Arougheti says Ares looked at about 160 viable use cases and is actively deploying about 25 across front, middle and back office

Named work includes almost fully automated NDA review, AML and KYC, Salesforce optimisation, investment teams using AI for committee memos and models, and ChatGPT, Copilot and Gemini rolled out systematically to desktops
Arougheti ties this to 2025 being the slowest organic headcount growth in over ten years; the July 2026 call repeats present-tense productivity AI and automation of RFPs, DDQs, AML and KYC
Confidence med: both sources are Ares executives speaking first-party, with no corroboration and no penetration or daily-use figure
Stops short of embedded: every named use case augments people who still own the work, and no source shows an investment decision without a human in the loop or the organisation redesigned around AI
Aberdeen Group (abrdn): Half-year 2026 report, July 2026, says AI is emerging as a meaningful enabler across the Group and that Copilot is being rolled out with strong adoption to date
CEO Jason Windsor says Copilot Premium is being rolled out and colleagues report meaningful time savings; every internal-adoption statement is first-party and uncorroborated
Governance documented earlier: the July 2024 University of Edinburgh research companion project sits under abrdn's AI Governance Framework

Stops short of scaling: the investment-process tool is still pre-production, an alpha test model and later prototype with no evidence of live research use, the assistant is described as rolling out rather than deployed, the two prior results announcements carried no internal-AI content, and Windsor's framing is forward-looking
Legal & General: H1 2026 call, August 2026: group CEO Antonio Simoes says L&G launched an AI-driven agent desktop in the retail business that is now driving efficiency improvements
L&G reported being the first large UK provider approved for the FCA targeted support regime, launched with AI-driven nudges supporting customer decisions

October 2025 Microsoft announcement documents Dynamics 365 Contact Center with Copilot transcription and case summaries, first phase covering workplace savings, retail protection and annuities across 12.4 million customers
June 2026 three-year expansion states L&G will continue to deploy Microsoft 365 Copilot to all 10,000 employees globally

Stops short of scaling: production use cases sit inside Retail, the Copilot deployment is described as continuing with no penetration figure, no AI appears in the asset-management investment process, and no policy, committee or responsible-AI framework was found
Ameriprise Financial: Q2 2026 call: CEO Jim Cracchiolo says e-meeting automation saves advisors 10 to 20 hours weekly, meeting summarization five to 10, Copilot Premium two and a half, with about 6,000 advisors already using them
Q1 2026 call describes AI deployed into everyday workflows across advice, operations and service on an integrated platform with a data foundation and governance
Q4 2025 call adds AI and intelligent automation in service, underwriting and asset-management transformation; all three sources are first-party, so confidence is med

Stops short of scaling: metricked deployments are advisor-facing and reported as an absolute count with no total or penetration rate, cross-segment mentions name no tool, governance is one passing reference, no AI is placed in Columbia Threadneedle's process, and further agents are future tense
DWS Group: Own quarterly results calls are the only public record, and describe readiness and experimentation rather than a shipped use case
FY2025 call, January 2026: CFO Markus Kobler says DWS exited its own cloud and migrated into Deutsche Bank's environment, freeing resources for automation and AI, a resourcing statement

Three months later CEO Stefan Hoops frames the firm as only now ready to apply AI to investment management after years ordering data and processes; Kobler cites a range of initiatives naming no tool, team, vendor or metric
Stops short of piloting: across four quarterly calls checked no named pilot, limited deployment, AI use policy or governance committee appears, and progressing a range of initiatives reads as intent
Victory Capital: Public AI record is organizational intent rather than deployment

March 2026 appointment of Molly Weiss as Chief Technology Officer and Head of Digital Innovation, an Executive Committee seat carrying responsibility for the AI framework and the data and analytics platform
Q2 2026 results call: Chairman and CEO David Brown lists AI among spending priorities alongside product development and technology

Stops short of piloting: no named pilot, internal tool, AI use policy or governance committee in any source read, no adoption figure, the AI framework is a responsibility being assigned, and the Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 calls mention AI not at all
J.P. Morgan Asset Management: January 2026: the firm cut ties with proxy advisers ISS and Glass Lewis to rely solely on Proxy IQ, an internal AI-driven voting platform for US shareholder voting, reported as the first such move by a major asset manager and set to handle data collection, research and recommendations

Two tools inside the investment process remain pilots by executives' own account: SpectrumGPT, a GPT-4 research-note drafter still being tested in October 2023, and Moneyball, a behavioural-bias tool still being developed in June 2024
Human authority explicit: the global head of data science says she remains the decision maker and accountable person

Stops short of scaling: neither SpectrumGPT nor Moneyball is shown reaching production, no penetration or daily-use figure exists for any of the three tools, no AM-specific policy or committee surfaced, and the current-tense platform claim sits on an undated own-domain page
Q1 2026 call: CEO Jon Winkelried says engineers in TPG's own tech group built LLM-based tools rolled out systematically to the firm
Winkelried claims approaching 80% of the firm now uses these tools on an active daily basis; a first-party figure that could not be corroborated externally
Lab 39, TPG's in-house AI team since 2019, built Samantha, an agentic platform used to interrogate the firm's own research and diligence data
TPG says the investment decision ultimately remains with the humans in the room, with AI a supplement to the discussion

Stops short of embedded: no autonomous decisions and no org redesign are claimed, and the assistant meant to give the investment committee a weekly risk and opportunity report is described in future tense, counted as intent
Manulife Investment Management: October 2025 release: the AI Research Assistant Platform is live in the public-markets investment process, synthesizing financials, sell-side commentary, internal notes, earnings transcripts and news into daily workflows
First-party metrics: 65% of public markets investment team members had incorporated it as of 31 August 2025, with document-mining time cut 70-80%; no independent corroboration

Governance published alongside: Responsible AI Principles covering responsible development, investment-led solutions and integrated risk and compliance oversight, with investment decisions reserved to the portfolio management team

Stops short of scaling: one production use case in the investment process, the three further tools shipped by May 2026 sit in advisor-compliance, retirement-distribution and retail-sales businesses, and the 75% GenAI engagement figure is parent-level across the insurer
AP Pension: Public AI record from 2023 onward is intent and enablement rather than deployment
Enterprise data foundation live on Microsoft Fabric per Microsoft's May 2024 customer story, which puts AI itself in the future as capabilities the organisation is keen to explore
Own newsroom announced a Festina Finance core system live from 1 May 2025 that the CIO says enables automated processes using AI, a platform making AI possible rather than a shipped use case

Stops short of piloting: no source names an AI system in production, a pilot in a named team, or a dated AI policy or committee, and the 2026 annual results make no AI claim while listing data use and automation among future priorities; confidence low
Colonial First State: Copilot went from 300 licences in January 2024 to 75% of employees having access by July 2024, per Microsoft's own account
CFS self-reported through Microsoft's newsroom that all pilot programme users believe Copilot saves them time, with 40% saving more than 30 minutes a day; no independent measurement

A five-year Microsoft agreement signed July 2024 names cloud and generative AI as strategic and itemises Azure OpenAI work: a FirstTech service trained on superannuation legislation documents, member-feedback analysis and contact-centre agent assistance

Stops short of scaling: only the enterprise assistant is evidenced as broadly used, the FirstTech service is confined to one team, remaining use cases are framed as working on and exploring, no AI sits in the investment process, and no policy or committee is disclosed
